AuditEntry.description: One thing the system did. Written by the audit hook, never by an agent.

action.description: Tool name, or the node's phase.
action.title: Action

AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry

CascadeResult.description:
A long-horizon ambition, cashed into goals that can actually be worked.

"A billion-dollar company in fifteen years" is not a task and pretending
otherwise produces a plan nobody believes. The Cascader walks it down one
rung at a time until something lands at a horizon that can hold a calendar
slot, and says honestly when it cannot.

goals.description: New goals, each with contributes_to set to the rung above it.
goals.title: Goals

rationale.description: Why this decomposition and not another.
rationale.title: Rationale

clarifying_questions.description: Ask rather than invent a plausible-sounding ladder. Empty when it was clear.
clarifying_questions.title: Clarifying Questions

CascadeResult.title: CascadeResult

CheckIn.description:
The daily reconciliation. What actually happened, from the only source that knows.

**This is not a notification.** It sits inside the brief the user is already
looking at, so it costs them nothing extra -- which is why it can be daily
without breaking the promise that Second stays quiet.

Without it the system's picture drifts: slips get inferred that never
happened, honoured slots get recorded as abandoned, and every diagnosis
downstream is built on a guess.

on.description: The day being reconciled, usually yesterday.
on.title: On

CheckIn.title: CheckIn

CheckInItem.description:
One thing to confirm, arriving with the answer already filled in.

Second does everything it can before asking. It knows what was scheduled, it
has looked for evidence, and it has formed a view. The user's job is one tap
to confirm or correct -- not to remember and report.

evidence.description: Why Second thinks so. Empty when it genuinely has nothing and is simply asking.
evidence.title: Evidence

CheckInItem.title: CheckInItem

CompletionReport.description:
The user's own answer about one task. Beats every inference.

When this disagrees with the Observer, this wins and the inference is
discarded -- not averaged, not weighed. The person was there.

note.description: Anything they said about why, in their words.
note.title: Note

CompletionReport.title: CompletionReport

DailyBrief.description:
What Second has for you today. The product's face.

Assembled every day, whether or not anything needs you. **Existing is not
interrupting** -- ``notify`` is the separate, rarer decision about whether to
push. Silence means ``notify`` is false and ``decisions`` is empty, not that
the brief is missing.

The order of the fields is the order of value: what you are doing, what has
already been done for you, what is slipping, what you forgot, and only then
what Second needs from you.

prepared.description: Work carried to the last click while the user was elsewhere.
prepared.title: Prepared

decisions.description: Usually empty. Each one costs the user attention, so earn it.
decisions.title: Decisions

check_in.description: Yesterday, pre-filled, awaiting confirmation. Does not trigger a notification.

notify.description: Push this at the user. True only when a decision is needed or something was prepared.
notify.title: Notify

silence_reason.description: When notify is false, why. Recorded for the audit, never shown to the user.
silence_reason.title: Silence Reason

DailyBrief.title: DailyBrief

Decision.description:
The one kind of thing that is allowed to interrupt.

Second reaches here only when it genuinely cannot proceed alone. Options are
included because a question with three researched answers costs five seconds
and a bare question costs a round trip.
Decision.title: Decision

Deprioritised.description: Something that lost the competition for a slot, and why it lost.

reason.description: Deadline pressure, a person-layer constraint, or an honoured-slot record.
reason.title: Reason

Deprioritised.title: Deprioritised

Diagnosis.description:
Why a task slipped, and whether Second can act on it alone.

``requires_user_decision`` routes the Daily Graph. It is a typed field read by
a conditional edge, not a prompt hoping for the best.

**``evidence`` is nullable, and that is load-bearing.** Strands produces
structured output by *forcing* a tool call: if the model declines, it is
re-asked with the choice forced, and on that pass it cannot refuse. A required
non-nullable ``evidence`` field would therefore compel the model to write
*something* in it even when nothing in the calendar or inbox supports a cause
-- which is how a real quote ends up attached to a conclusion it does not
support. The rule this model is meant to encode, *no evidence no diagnosis*,
is precisely the rule forced tool choice removes. So the schema has to give
the model somewhere honest to land.

evidence.description: Quote the calendar entry or the email this rests on. Leave null if nothing in the evidence supports a structural cause. Never invent or paraphrase a quote to fill this field.
evidence.title: Evidence

requires_user_decision.description: True when Second genuinely cannot resolve this without the user.
requires_user_decision.title: Requires User Decision

Diagnosis.title: Diagnosis

ExtractionResult.description: What the Extractor heard in a spoken brain dump.

goals.description: One per distinct thing the user wants. Shallow: no routes yet.
goals.title: Goals

clarifying_questions.description: Ask rather than guess. Empty when everything was clear.
clarifying_questions.title: Clarifying Questions

ExtractionResult.title: ExtractionResult

FeedbackResult.description:
Everything the Interpreter took from one thing the user said.

Covers both directions of the daily loop: ``completions`` is the user
reporting backwards on what actually happened, ``updates`` is everything else
-- a preference, a time that does not work, a route that is too much.

completions.description: Answers to the check-in. Ground truth; overrides what was inferred.
completions.title: Completions

intentions.description: Things the user says they want to do today that are not yet in the plan.
intentions.title: Intentions

acknowledgement.description: At most one line back to the user. Often empty.
acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement

FeedbackResult.title: FeedbackResult

FeedbackUpdate.description: One typed change derived from something the user said back.

change.description: What to change, in terms the Adapter can act on.
change.title: Change

person_model_patch.description: Merged into PersonModel.preferences. This is how Second learns.
person_model_patch.title: Person Model Patch

FeedbackUpdate.title: FeedbackUpdate

Goal.description:
Something the user said they want, at some distance from today.

Goals form a ladder rather than a list. "A billion-dollar company in fifteen
years" is a real goal and it is not a task; it becomes a three-year goal,
which becomes this year's, which becomes something that occupies Tuesday
morning. ``contributes_to`` is that ladder, and it is what lets Second answer
the only question that matters on a Tuesday morning: *why this, today?*

contributes_to.description: The id of the longer-horizon goal this serves. None for a top-level ambition.
contributes_to.title: Contributes To

extraction_confidence.description: How sure the Extractor was that this is a real, distinct goal.
extraction_confidence.title: Extraction Confidence

Goal.title: Goal

GoalStatusChange.description:
What pausing or retiring a goal actually did.

``freed`` is the point. Retiring a goal releases the calendar time its routes
were holding, and the Goals screen has to be able to show that concretely --
these slots, this many hours, no longer spoken for.

It says *freed*, not *redistributed*, deliberately. The Scheduler has not run
again yet, so nothing has been reallocated. Claiming otherwise would have
Second describing a plan it has not made, which is the one thing this product
must never do. ``note`` says when the reallocation actually happens.

freed.description: Upcoming slots the goal was holding, now released. Empty when it held none.
freed.title: Freed

note.description: What becomes of the freed time, in plain words.
note.title: Note

GoalStatusChange.title: GoalStatusChange

IntakeResult.description:
What one spoken brain dump produced.

``clarifying_questions`` being non-empty means the Intake graph stopped after
the Extractor on purpose: it was not clear enough what the user wanted to
justify putting anything in their calendar. ``schedule`` is ``None`` in that
case, and the caller asks rather than shows a plan.

schedule.description: What the Scheduler placed and what it deprioritised, when it ran.

IntakeResult.title: IntakeResult

Link.description: An edge between the goals layer and the person layer.

from_id.description: Goals-layer id: a goal, route or task.
from_id.title: From Id

to_ref.description: Person-layer reference: a preference key, slot or constraint.
to_ref.title: To Ref

Link.title: Link

LivingGraph.description:
One persistent structure per user. Written by every agent, read by every agent.

``version`` backs the conditional write that stops two nodes in the same run
clobbering each other. Read it, send it back with your update, and expect the
write to be rejected if it moved underneath you.
LivingGraph.title: LivingGraph

Observation.description:
What the Observer could work out about one scheduled slot.

Inference only. The calendar can show an invite was declined and the inbox
can show a mail was never sent, but **nothing in either can tell you whether
somebody actually did the five-minute recording.** That is what the check-in
is for, and it is why ``outcome`` is allowed to be ``"unknown"`` rather than
being forced into a guess.

evidence.description: Quote the calendar entry or the email. No evidence, no claim.
evidence.title: Evidence

Observation.title: Observation

ObservationReport.description:
The Observer's sanitised bundle. The only thing the Diagnostician sees.

This is the context-isolation boundary made concrete: the Observer reads raw
calendar entries and raw email, and hands on **this** -- task ids, outcomes
and quoted evidence. Not inbox contents. The Diagnostician cannot reach
Gmail or Calendar itself, so this report is the whole of its world.

notes.description: Structural context not tied to one task, e.g. a standing meeting that moved.
notes.title: Notes

ObservationReport.title: ObservationReport

PersonModel.description:
Observed facts about how this person actually operates.

Structural only. Every field here is something the system watched happen, or
something the user said outright. Nothing in this model is an inference about
motivation, discipline or mood, and no agent may write one.

constraints.description: Hard rules the Scheduler must honour, e.g. "no work before 10am".
constraints.title: Constraints

honoured_slots.description: Time slots this person actually keeps, e.g. "Tue 07:00".
honoured_slots.title: Honoured Slots

abandoned_slots.description: Slots repeatedly scheduled and repeatedly missed.
abandoned_slots.title: Abandoned Slots

resources_served.description: Already shown to the user. The Resource Finder never repeats one.
resources_served.title: Resources Served

PersonModel.title: PersonModel

Placement.description: One task placed into a real calendar slot.
Placement.title: Placement

PreparedAction.description:
Work carried up to the last click, and stopped there.

Second never completes the irreversible step. A draft is created, never sent.
Options are assembled, never booked.

summary.description: What was prepared, in one line.
summary.title: Summary

detail.description: The draft body, the compared options, the retrieved value.
detail.title: Detail

external_ref.description: Gmail draft id, calendar event id.
external_ref.title: External Ref

awaiting.description: The single thing left for the user to do.
awaiting.title: Awaiting

PreparedAction.title: PreparedAction

Reminder.description:
Something the user cares about and has probably forgotten.

Not a nag and not a nudge. This exists because commitments get made in email
and then never reach a plan -- a reply promised, a form nobody filled in, a
booking that closes. Every one cites where it came from, and a reminder with
no evidence is a defect.
Reminder.title: Reminder

Risk.description: Something with a deadline that will not be met on the current plan.

evidence.description: Why this is at risk. Cite the calendar or the graph.
evidence.title: Evidence

Risk.title: Risk

Route.description: One concrete way of reaching a goal. Proposed by Second, approved by the user.

cadence.description: How often, in plain words. 'Weekly, Tuesday evenings'.
cadence.title: Cadence

rationale.description: Why this route suits THIS person, citing a person-layer fact.
rationale.title: Rationale

Route.title: Route

RoutePlan.description:
Concrete routes proposed for goals that are near enough to work on.

Shallow on purpose. The alternative was to carry whole ``Goal`` objects here,
which means a Goal->Route->Task schema at every hop and nothing persisted at
all if the Scheduler fails downstream. Instead the Cascader writes the goal
ladder to the graph as it goes, and this carries only what is new -- so a
scheduling failure costs the routes, not the ladder.

routes.description: Proposed routes, each already bound to a goal_id.
routes.title: Routes

rationale.description: Why these routes suit THIS person, citing a person-layer fact.
rationale.title: Rationale

clarifying_questions.description: Ask rather than invent a cadence the user will abandon in week two.
clarifying_questions.title: Clarifying Questions

RoutePlan.title: RoutePlan

ScheduleDecision.description:
The Scheduler's verdict across ALL active goals at once.

``deprioritised`` is not optional output. A scheduler that only reports what
it placed is hiding the decision it actually made.

rationale.description: How competition between goals was resolved.
rationale.title: Rationale

ScheduleDecision.title: ScheduleDecision

ScheduledBlock.description:
One piece of work occupying a real slot today, and what it is for.

``goal_title`` and ``serves`` are denormalised onto the block on purpose. The
day has to answer *why this, today?* without the reader following a chain of
ids, and "Draft the pitch — 45 min — serves: speak well → this year → the
decade" is the whole product in one line.

serves.description: Titles of the longer-horizon goals above this one, nearest first.
serves.title: Serves

start.description: Timezone-AWARE, in the user's own zone. Note the asymmetry, which is deliberate: Task.scheduled_slots are stored NAIVE because the Living Graph holds wall-clock time -- a plan is what the person reads off their own calendar, and storing it as UTC would move the plan when they travel. Anything crossing the API boundary is made aware by Clock.local() so a browser cannot guess wrong. Never compare a raw scheduled_slot against one of these without passing it through the clock first.
start.title: Start

resource_url.description: Material attached to the slot, so the thing to watch is already there.
resource_url.title: Resource Url

ScheduledBlock.title: ScheduledBlock

Slip.description: One occasion on which a task did not happen as planned.
Slip.title: Slip

Task.description: A single concrete action inside a route.

depends_on.description: Task ids that must be done first. An UNMET_DEPENDENCY diagnosis reads this.
depends_on.title: Depends On

known_blocker.description: Written from the user's own answer. Once set, never ask about this task again.
known_blocker.title: Known Blocker

resource_url.description: Material attached to this task's slot, so it is already there at 7am.
resource_url.title: Resource Url

Task.title: Task
